body: I'd like to highlight one more issue with colors in the modern theme - the font color of currently active view switcher is pure black (as in hex 000000). Most designers will agree that using pure black or pure white usually results in a too harsh contrast that is not pleasant for the eyes. Furthermore, from what I can see it's the only place in the editor where pure white is being used, so it's not consistent as well. Other active tabs have a slightly gray font color: I also checked the dark theme and it also uses pure white, although at least for my eyes it's effect seems a little bit less harsh here: There could be a few ways to solve this issue, here's some that come to my mind: 1. Make the active font color less harsh, decrease contrast for inactive. I'm just not sure if current Godot's design system would make it obvious at a glance weather decreased contrast font indicates inactive or disabled/inaccessible state. 2. Make the active font use accent color. I think it would work well, as it already works well in the classic theme. But maybe it would introduce an unwanted inconsistency, as from what I can see there was a decision to decrease the usage of accent colors for fonts in the modern theme. (BTW now that I'm looking at my screenshots - why is one of the files in the FileSystem inspector tab have it's font color set to the accent color? It's not immediately obvious for me and is perhaps another issue) 3. Make the active tab have a different background color. I think this could work well and would be consistent with the current existing design, as for example the entries in the menu bar (Scene, Project, Debug, ...) get a background color when selected.
